paragraphs.heading: Final week, final lesson
paragraphs.edited: All right, you did it. This is the final week, the final lesson of this incredible year of studying apologetics and preparing your students to be one step closer to being entirely confident — to walk across the stage of graduation and to engage their culture with the truth of the gospel. I can't express how excited I am to hear the stories of our students and what they've been able to experience, and the stories of students who started off with skepticism and doubt and have been brought along into committed followers of Christ, proclaiming the gospel far beyond the walls of your youth group. So I'm excited, and I hope you're excited too.

paragraphs.heading: Take an inventory
paragraphs.edited: The second thing is to take some time to do an inventory. Go back to when you first started talking, and go back to where your students were. Have your students go back to where they were, and invite them to think it through: what was I thinking back then? Have them go back to their notes. What were you thinking in lesson 1.1 versus how you're thinking now, when the concept of apologetics was first introduced? The questions you had way back in the beginning — have those questions been answered now? What further questions do you have? Where do we go from here? How do we continue to move on?

paragraphs.heading: Successes and failures
paragraphs.edited: The next thing is successes and failures. For your storyteller, you want someone who can tell a great story about sharing the truth. But keep this in mind: you don't necessarily want somebody who successfully shared the gospel every time. Students are going to need to see some examples of falling flat on their face, because they probably are going to, and that's okay. Maybe that's a good thing, because you generally learn a lot more from failure than you do from successes. So have somebody who can express both sides, especially if you can find somebody who failed, learned from that failure, and moved on to some success.

paragraphs.heading: God gives the growth
paragraphs.edited: Keep in mind, and remind your students time and again, that it's not us who does the saving. It is God's job. I have an analogy I've often given students: they're all going to be in different places, and God is going to have all different kinds of roles for them. Some water, some plant, but it's God who causes the growth. And I often talk about the wide range of jobs, from excavation to tree shaking.

paragraphs.heading: Encourage your students
paragraphs.edited: So just remember to encourage your students that wherever they are on that spectrum, to be faithful to the gifts and talents God has given them. They are going to face some challenges. They are going to face questions they don't have answers to all the time, and they're going to have to seek those answers out. They are also going to have awesome success, and they're going to get the thrill of leading someone to know Christ.
